title: Alterations of Neuromuscular Function after the World's Most Challenging Mountain Ultra-Marathon
authors: Saugy J, Place N, Millet GY, Degache F, Schena F, Millet GP
population: 15 experienced ultra-marathon runners in a 330 km, 24,000 m elevation-change trail race (finish time 122.43 +/- 17.21 h) and 8 sleep-deprived controls
findings: Maximal voluntary contraction declined -13 +/- 17% (knee extensors) and -10 +/- 16% (plantar flexors) at mid-race and -24 +/- 13% and -26 +/- 19% post-race; central activation ratio fell -24 +/- 24% and -28 +/- 34%; controls did not change.
Peripheral markers also altered: 100 Hz doublet -18 +/- 18% (KE) and -20 +/- 15% (PF); peak twitch -33 +/- 12% (KE) and -19 +/- 14% (PF).
Post-race CK 3719 +/- 3045 U/L, LDH 1145 +/- 511, CRP 13.1 +/- 7.5 mg/L and myoglobin 449.3 +/- 338.2 ug/L, all higher than pre-race in runners but not controls.

Authors report less neuromuscular fatigue, muscle damage and inflammation than in shorter mountain ultras, and conclude such extreme exercise seems to induce a relative muscle preservation process, likely due to protective anticipatory pacing and sleep deprivation.
limitations: No post-race recovery time course in the abstract; very small sample of highly experienced finishers at slow paces; the comparison with shorter ultras is indirect.
implications: Damage and neuromuscular deficit did not rise in proportion to distance: a 330 km event at slow pace produced smaller CK than the 166 km race (Millet 2011), though the deficit was still about -24 to -26% MVC. A hold that grows linearly with distance beyond 100 miles is not supported; a cap is a judgement, not a finding.

Because this paper has no recovery data, it cannot support a specific day count for races above 100 miles; using the 100-mile hold as the ceiling for events up to 330 km is a design choice that should be flagged as such.

verification.notes: Crossref (2013-06-26, authors match) and abstract re-read (PMID 23840345); all numbers match. Implication reworded so the cap is labelled a judgement and the residual deficit is stated.
